labels.name: Sayyidna Tuan Muhammad Said
labels.profileTitle: Islamic scholar · early Hajj pilgrim of Lanao

biography.heading: Kawashima Midori: pilgrimage and Islamic learning
biography.summary: Known locally as Kadi (or Hadi) sa Binidayan, Sayyidna Tuan Muhammad Said is studied by Kawashima Midori through local oral accounts and manuscripts of the early nineteenth century.

facts.text: Kawashima’s 2017 paper reports an oral account describing Sayyidna as one of the earliest Hajj pilgrims from the Lake Lanao area.

In that account, Sayyidna was the first person from southern Lake Lanao to study Islam in Mecca for an extended period and return safely. This is a narrower claim than being the first Hajj pilgrim of the Philippines.
Kawashima’s 2019 chapter, Connecting Mindanao to Hijaz, continues the study of Sayyidna’s journey.

biography.identityNote: The English badge “Pioneer Hajj Pilgrim” reflects the qualified oral-tradition account. The separate chart entry Tuan sa Binidayan is not merged with this scholar. The research does not independently authenticate all family links in this chart.

labels.name: Samurong
labels.transcriptionNote: Grandchild of Maruhom through one unnamed parent, according to the family account. Reported full first cousin of the earlier Dimaporo entry, displayed at the same level for diagram layout. The shared ancestors remain unresolved; the recorded paths from Maruhom differ by one step. According to the family account, Samurong’s mother was Malaysian. Her name and specific ethnicity are not yet known. It is not established whether that mother is the child of Maruhom. Correction recorded in the archive: Samurong is a woman. Ginaronai from Poon a Baebao was her second spouse; their child is Calanda Ginaronai. The earlier attribution of Bayango as her child was corrected. Alicasan, November 9, 2026: Samurong and the unnamed mother of Usman Imam are cousins through their mothers. The cousin degree and common ancestors remain unspecified.

additionalAccounts.note: Samurong and the mother of Usman Imam are cousins through their mothers; degree and common ancestors unspecified.

labels.name: Ginaronai
labels.transcriptionNote: Ginaronai (also spelled Ginaronay) was a man from Poon a Baebao, the second husband of Samurong, and the father of Calanda Ginaronai, according to the family account.
labels.profileTitle: Husband of Samurong · Father of Calanda Ginaronai

labels.name: Bayango Gandamazir
labels.transcriptionNote: According to the corrected family account, Bayango Gandamazir comes from the Digadong lineage; the intervening ancestors and generation count are unknown. Connected partner and reported second cousin of Calanda Ginaronai; their shared ancestor remains unresolved. Bayango is not recorded as a child of Samurong. The existing main family diagram names Gandamasir as Bayango’s father; a family informant identifies Gandamasir as a child of Tuan sa Magonaya, who was a child of Hadji Said. According to Alicasan, November 9, 2026, Bayango Gandamasir and Calanda Ginaronai are second cousins through the Digadong family. Their common ancestor and intervening ancestry have not yet been identified; this is a reported family relationship, not a calculated or independently verified kinship result.

labels.name: Calanda Ginaronai
labels.transcriptionNote: According to the corrected family account, Calanda Ginaronai is the child of Samurong and Ginaronai from Poon a Baebao. Calanda is recorded as the partner of Bayango Gandamazir. Bayango and Calanda are reported second cousins; their common ancestor remains unresolved. According to Alicasan Calanda, Calanda Ginaronai travelled to Manila to sell peanuts. The date, route, vessel and length of stay are not yet known. This oral account is open for research in passenger lists, port or shipping records and other relevant archives; no matching record has yet been identified. According to Alicasan, November 9, 2026, Bayango Gandamasir and Calanda Ginaronai are second cousins through the Digadong family. Their common ancestor and intervening ancestry have not yet been identified; this is a reported family relationship, not a calculated or independently verified kinship result. Mohamad Ali Dimaporo and Calanda Ginaronai are reported second cousins in the family account. Their shared ancestors and connecting ancestry are not yet identified. This refers to Mohamad Ali Dimaporo (chart-132), not the earlier Sultan Dimaporo (chart-126).

biography.heading: Usman Imam Sheik Al-Aman · Kawashima Midori / Sophia reference
biography.summary: Kawashima’s commentary on Usman Imam’s lecture identifies his parents and distinguishes the generation statement about his father.

facts.text: Section II.1 identifies Tabunawan as Usman Imam’s father and as the imam of the village mosque. The place appears as マゴナナ (Magonana) in the Japanese text.
The father, Tabunawan, is described as Sayyidna’s sixth-generation descendant. This statement does not assign the sixth generation to Usman Imam.
Usman’s unnamed mother is described as coming from Bayang. The commentary records Usman as born in 1943.

biography.identityNote: Mamadra, the half-brother connection to Calanda Ginaronai, and the maternal-cousin connection to Samurong are attributed to Alicasan, November 9, 2026. The intermediate ancestors between Sayyidna and Tabunawan are not named in this passage. The repository is under maintenance; local notes preserve short source excerpts and a summary, not the original PDF.

sources.title: Kawashima Midori, commentary on Usman Imam’s lecture, section II.1 · original Sophia PDF

additionalAccounts.note: Mamadra is Usman’s sibling. Usman’s mother and Samurong are cousins through their mothers.
